chapter_name: Elements of Art: Line, Shape, Color, Texture, Space
learning_objective: 🎯 Master the fundamental building blocks of visual arts and understand how artists use them to create masterpieces!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A line is a mark made by a moving point. It can be straight, curvy, thick, or thin. Lines are used to outline shapes, create shading (hatching), and guide the viewer's eye.
Shapes are flat (2D) enclosed areas. Geometric shapes (circles, squares) are precise and mathematical. Organic shapes (leaves, clouds) are free-flowing and found in nature.
Colors bring life to art. Primary colors (Red, Blue, Yellow) cannot be mixed from other colors. Secondary colors (Green, Orange, Purple) are made by mixing two primary colors.
Texture is how a surface feels (tactile) or looks like it feels (visual). An artist can paint a surface to look rough like tree bark or smooth like glass.
Positive space is the actual object or subject in the artwork. Negative space is the empty area around and between the subjects. Both are equally important for a balanced composition.

fun_activity.title: 🪵 The Texture Rubbing Hunt
fun_activity.instructions: Take a piece of paper and a crayon. Walk around your house or garden and place the paper over different surfaces (leaves, coins, brick walls) and rub the crayon over it. See how many visual textures you can collect!

exam_tips: 📌 Always define 'Line' as a moving dot. It is the most basic element of art.
📌 Differentiate clearly between Geometric shapes (man-made, precise) and Organic shapes (natural, irregular).
📌 Remember the Color Wheel: Primary colors mix to create Secondary colors.
quick_recap: ⭐ The elements of art are the visual tools artists use to create a composition.
⭐ Warm colors (red, orange, yellow) pop out, while cool colors (blue, green, purple) recede into the background.
⭐ Texture can be real (you can touch it) or implied (an illusion created by the artist).
